title: Towards Improving Sequential Decision-Making in LLM Agents via Experience Memory
title_zh: 通过经验记忆改进 LLM Agent 的序贯决策能力

author_affiliations.name: Jakub Rada
affiliations: AI Center, Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague

author_affiliations.name: Viliam Lisý
affiliations: AI Center, Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague

abstract_en: Large language models have improved substantially on single-shot reasoning tasks, but their performance in sequential decision-making is less well understood. We study this on fully-observable two-player zero-sum games, which provide ground-truth evaluation: outcomes are determined by the rules, and optimality of individual moves can be computed or approximated, without relying on a judge model. Across model tiers, LLMs play suboptimally in simple games such as tic-tac-toe or Connect Four, and lose to MCTS opponents. Obfuscations that preserve the game tree but rewrite its surface form leave performance largely unchanged, indicating the gap is not fully explained by recall of memorized strategies. Motivated by this performance gap, we introduce an agentic framework enhanced with an experience memory designed for the sequential setting and addressing common challenges of sequential decision-making such as credit assignment. We show that post-game reflection and rule extraction yield measurable improvements on tic-tac-toe without modifying the model weights.
abstract_zh: 本文研究大语言模型（LLM）在序贯决策任务中的表现，重点分析完全可观测的双人零和游戏场景，如 tic-tac-toe 和 Connect Four。这类游戏具有明确规则与可验证结果，可直接计算或近似评估单步动作的最优性，无需依赖 judge model。实验发现，不同能力层级的 LLM 在简单游戏中仍会做出次优决策，并常输给 MCTS 对手。即使对游戏表层形式进行改写、但保持游戏树不变，模型表现也基本不变，说明性能差距不能简单归因于是否记住了策略。针对这一问题，作者提出一种带有 experience memory 的 agentic framework，用于处理序贯决策中的信用分配等挑战。结果表明，在不修改模型权重的情况下，赛后反思与规则抽取能在 tic-tac-toe 上带来可测量的性能提升。
key_points_zh: 论文系统评估 LLM 在完全可观测双人零和游戏中的序贯决策能力，使用规则结果和动作最优性作为客观评估依据。
实验显示，即使在 tic-tac-toe、Connect Four 等简单游戏中，LLM 仍频繁做出次优动作，并会输给 MCTS 对手。
通过对游戏表层形式进行混淆但保持 game tree 不变，作者发现模型表现变化不大，说明问题并非主要来自记忆策略缺失或表面文本差异。
作者提出带有 experience memory 的 agentic framework，通过赛后反思、经验存储和规则抽取来缓解序贯决策中的 credit assignment 问题。
在不更新模型权重的前提下，该方法在 tic-tac-toe 上取得可测量提升，展示了经验记忆对 LLM Agent 决策改进的潜力。

llm_assessment.comment: Experience memory is relevant to Agent memory, but the contribution appears narrow and tied to simple sequential games with reflection-style updates.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 经验记忆与 Agent Memory 相关，但贡献较窄，主要绑定于简单序贯博弈和反思式更新。
